clue.text: Openings in Commonwealth area involving a Commonwealth state

indicators.note: to involve is to take in, so the phrase built from the openings wraps round the single letter

parts.note: the openings, or first letters, of the two words Commonwealth and area are C and A, written out with the joining word

explanation.surface: Vacancies in a Commonwealth region concern one particular member nation.
explanation.walkthrough: The trick is to spell out 'C and A' in full, conjunction included, then slip the extra A inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: A North American nation that is a member of the Commonwealth of Nations, with the British monarch as head of state.

clue.text: Sequential description of discussions in defence?

definitions.meaning: one after another, consecutive, like wins in successive matches
in football the defenders are the backs, so talks between them are one back speaking to another

explanation.surface: A puzzled attempt to describe how defenders confer with each other during a match.
explanation.walkthrough: The second reading is whimsical: a chat among defensive players is literally one 'back' talking to another.
explanation.definitionFit: Events happening consecutively, with no gap between them, are commonly said to come in this fashion.

clue.text: Fabric Queen twice displayed in legal action

indicators.note: the royal letters are shown inside the lawsuit word, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: a legal action is a case brought in court
the Queen is abbreviated two ways, HM (Her Majesty) and ER (Elizabeth Regina), giving both

explanation.surface: A cloth with royal connections features prominently in a court case.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Queen twice' means two different abbreviations for the monarch, not the same one repeated.
explanation.definitionFit: This is a fine soft wool from Kashmir goats, woven into luxurious cloth.

clue.text: Put on a show for father instead of turning up for crossword?

indicators.note: the father word takes the place of the flipped short word, signalling a swap of letters

parts.note: a crossword is a puzzle

indicators.note: turning means the little word up is read backwards

parts.note: taken as written before being turned
DA is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Someone shows off for their dad rather than turning up for a crossword session.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turning up' makes PU, which is replaced in PUZZLE by DA.
explanation.definitionFit: To impress spectators with brilliance is to perform showily, making a dramatic display.

clue.text: Amusing to be around a pastoral deity

indicators.note: the fun word surrounds the single letter, so one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: something amusing is fun

explanation.surface: A merry country god capers about, enjoying himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman woodland spirit, half man and half goat, protector of shepherds and fields.

clue.text: A South American once enthralled by Egyptian god in religious epic

indicators.note: being held captive by the god means sitting inside his name

parts.note: Ra is the Egyptian sun god
the Maya were an ancient civilisation of the Americas, so a member was a Mayan

explanation.surface: An ancient American native falls under the spell of an Egyptian deity in a sacred saga.
explanation.walkthrough: The Maya actually lived in Central America; the setter's 'South American' is loose.
explanation.definitionFit: A Sanskrit Hindu epic poem recounting the life of Prince Rama.

clue.text: A chap apparently back in the country

indicators.note: back means the assembled pieces are read in reverse order

parts.note: a chap is a man
AP is a shortened form of apparently, as dictionaries abbreviate it

explanation.surface: A fellow seemingly returning home to his native land.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface nods to the famous palindrome 'A man, a plan, a canal: Panama'.
explanation.definitionFit: A Central American nation famous for its canal linking the Atlantic and Pacific.

clue.text: Repeatedly stove's beginning to ruin jelly

indicators.note: the assembled short piece is written out twice in a row

parts.note: an Aga is a British make of cast-iron range cooker

indicators.note: only the opening letter of the next word is taken

explanation.surface: A cook keeps finding that the stove ruins the jelly they are setting.
explanation.walkthrough: AGA is a heavy kitchen range found in many British country houses.
explanation.definitionFit: A gelatinous substance from seaweed, used to set foods and culture bacteria.

clue.text: Getting on, having provided billet for soldiers? Certainly

indicators.note: to billet troops is to lodge them, so the soldiers are housed within the other word

parts.note: someone getting on in years is aged
RE stands for the Royal Engineers, a British army corps

explanation.surface: An elderly householder, asked if they put up the troops, answers yes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Getting on' looks like the definition (agreeing well) but is the old-age container.
explanation.definitionFit: Used as an interjection, this word expresses assent, much like saying of course.

clue.text: Rating bowler's target

definitions.meaning: a rating is an ordinary sailor
in lawn bowls the small white ball aimed at

explanation.surface: Assessing a bowler's aim at their target.
explanation.definitionFit: A seaman is traditionally a tar, and the small target ball in lawn bowls has this name.

clue.text: TV science programme leading discussion mostly on the level

parts.note: Horizon is a long-running BBC science documentary series

indicators.note: most of the word is used, its final letter dropped

parts.note: a discussion is a talk

explanation.surface: A TV science show's opening debate is calm and even-handed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on the level' suggests honesty, but here means flat.
explanation.definitionFit: Lying flat, parallel to the ground, is the literal sense of being level.

clue.text: Colouring agent is something recalled in bamboo?

indicators.note: the memorised piece is placed within the stem word

parts.note: a bamboo stem is a cane
rote is material learned and recalled by repetition

explanation.surface: Wondering whether a dye was something remembered from bamboo.
explanation.definitionFit: An orange pigment found in carrots and other plants, giving them colour.

clue.text: Minor performers no longer rubbish? Not entirely

parts.note: ex means former, no longer

indicators.note: the rubbish word loses its last letter, so it is incomplete

parts.note: rubbish is trash

explanation.surface: Bit-part actors protest they are no longer rubbish, at least not completely.
explanation.definitionFit: Film walk-on people who appear in crowd scenes without lines.

clue.text: Exaggerated consequence of chewing that eclair

indicators.note: chewing mashes the letters up, so what results is a rearrangement

explanation.surface: Someone overreacts dramatically after munching a cream pastry.
explanation.definitionFit: Overdone and showy, as if performed on a stage.

clue.text: Flower, one found in US state meadow

indicators.note: the single letter is discovered sitting inside the combined state and field letters

parts.note: AZ is the postal abbreviation for Arizona
lea is a poetic word for a meadow
a means one

explanation.surface: A single bloom spotted in an American field.
explanation.definitionFit: A flowering shrub related to rhododendrons, grown for its showy blooms.

clue.text: A research centre: graduate brought on board by an American resident

parts.note: a lab, short for laboratory

indicators.note: taken aboard means placed inside, so the degree goes within the two-letter word

parts.note: taken as written
an MA is a Master of Arts graduate

explanation.surface: A lab takes on a graduate from an American.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone living in a particular southern US state, a native or inhabitant there.

clue.text: Nuisance besetting European with a dated currency

indicators.note: to beset is to surround, so the nuisance wraps round the single letter

parts.note: a nuisance is a pest

explanation.surface: A troublesome person bothers a European about old money.
explanation.definitionFit: Spain's former monetary unit before the euro replaced it in 2002.

clue.text: Elevated title capturing most suitable figure in morality

indicators.note: the flipped title holds the other piece inside it
in a down entry, raised means read from bottom to top, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: a title is a name
very as an adjective means exactly right, as in the very thing

explanation.surface: A lofty title is given to the most fitting person in an ethical tale.
explanation.walkthrough: 'morality' is short for a morality play, a medieval allegorical drama.
explanation.definitionFit: The allegorical hero of a famous fifteenth-century English morality play representing all humankind.

clue.text: Supplied golden colour on a hat

parts.note: supplied food means fed
or is the heraldic term for gold

explanation.surface: Someone provides a gold tint for a piece of headwear.
explanation.definitionFit: A soft felt brimmed headpiece with a crease along the crown.

clue.text: Restraint removing front feather from cockerel

indicators.note: the opening letter of the restraint word is taken away

parts.note: a shackle is a restraint for wrists or ankles

explanation.surface: A restraint is taken off, freeing a feather from a rooster.
explanation.definitionFit: A long, narrow plume on the neck of a domestic bird, raised when angry.

clue.text: Oratorio, I judge, with sound rising around

indicators.note: the healthy word wraps round the other two letters
in a down entry, rising means the word runs from bottom to top, so it is reversed

parts.note: sound in the sense of healthy means hale

explanation.surface: A judge reviews a choral work as its music swells about them.
explanation.definitionFit: Mendelssohn's famous choral work about the Old Testament prophet.

clue.text: Ultimate issue: gold brought back in clutches of the Spanish

indicators.note: held in the grip of the article, so the other pieces sit inside it

parts.note: el is Spanish for the
to vent is to issue or let out

indicators.note: brought back means the chemical symbol is read in reverse

parts.note: Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: The final outcome: Spaniards seize gold and return it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'issue' looks like a noun meaning outcome, beside 'Ultimate', but it is the verb to let out.
explanation.definitionFit: Happening at the end of a process, finally resulting.

clue.text: A river? Skill needed to secure a landing-point

indicators.note: the skill word holds the single letter safely inside it

parts.note: art means skill

explanation.surface: Steering down a river takes skill to reach a safe mooring.
explanation.definitionFit: The Turkish mountain where Noah's ark came to rest after the Flood.

clue.text: On a mystic bent, adopting new expression of holiness

indicators.note: the scrambled letters take in the extra letter, holding it inside
bent means twisted, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone with a mystical leaning takes up a fresh show of piety.
explanation.definitionFit: A pretended or self-righteous display of piety, holier-than-thou behaviour.

clue.text: Grasp lead item in constitutional legislation

indicators.note: the leading letter of the following word is taken

parts.note: legislation is law

explanation.surface: Understanding the main item in a constitutional bill.
explanation.definitionFit: To seize with hooked nails, gripping tightly.

clue.text: Country air damaged court card

indicators.note: damaged letters are broken up and rearranged

parts.note: Q is the queen in a pack of cards

explanation.surface: A nation's air quality damaged a royal card game.
explanation.definitionFit: A Middle Eastern nation with Baghdad as its capital.

clue.text: Prince recalled a cheering cry in a fix

indicators.note: called back means the whole assembly is read in reverse
the cheer goes inside the predicament

parts.note: a fix is a jam
rah is a cheer, as in hurrah

explanation.surface: A prince remembers a cheer while in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' puts ARAH within AJAM to give AJARAHAM, which 'recalled' reverses.
explanation.definitionFit: An Indian ruler or great king, a title above raja.

clue.text: Cheers, after bringing about a change: ditching unknown gaming figure

indicators.note: bringing about here means wrapping round, so the shortened piece encloses the thanks word
ditching means discarding, so one letter is dropped

parts.note: to change is to vary
Y is an algebraic unknown
ta is British slang for thanks, like cheers

explanation.surface: After a toast, a game figure undergoes a makeover, dropping something mysterious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ditching unknown' removes Y from AVARY; 'bringing about' wraps AVAR round TA.
explanation.definitionFit: A character representing a player in a video game or online world.
